name: christianpure-easter-moons
title: The Easter moon and the real moon, AD 325 to 2100
description: For every year from AD 325 to 2100: the full moon the church's Easter tables use (Julian every year, Gregorian from 1583), the real spring equinox and full moon as seen from Jerusalem, Western, Orthodox and astronomical (1997 Aleppo proposal) Easter, how many days each table's moon sits from the real one, and how many weeks apart the two Easters fall. From JPL DE441 through Skyfield. Dedicated to the public domain under CC0.

sources.title: JPL planetary and lunar ephemeris DE441: Park, R. S., Folkner, W. M., Williams, J. G., and Boggs, D. H. 2021. The JPL Planetary and Lunar Ephemerides DE440 and DE441. Astronomical Journal 161:105
Skyfield 1.55, Brandon Rhodes (Astrophysics Source Code Library ascl:1907.024)
Yallop, B. D. 1997. A Method for Predicting the First Sighting of the New Crescent Moon. NAO Technical Note 69, HM Nautical Almanac Office
Morrison, L. V., and Stephenson, F. R. 2004. Historical values of the Earth's clock error Delta T and the calculation of eclipses. Journal for the History of Astronomy 35:327-336 (the Delta T margin)

Morrison, L. V., Stephenson, F. R., Hohenkerk, C. Y., and Zawilski, M. 2021. Addendum 2020 to Measurement of the Earth's rotation: 720 BC to AD 2015. Proceedings of the Royal Society A 477:20200776 (Delta T itself, as Skyfield uses it)
Stephenson, F. R., Morrison, L. V., and Hohenkerk, C. Y. 2016. Measurement of the Earth's rotation: 720 BC to AD 2015. Proceedings of the Royal Society A 472:20160404 (Delta T before 720 BC)
Espenak, F., and Meeus, J. Five Millennium Canon of Lunar Eclipses and Five Millennium Catalog of Moon Phases, NASA (the checks)

resources.name: easter-moons
resources.title: Easter moons
resources.description: One row per year, AD 325 to 2100.

fields.name: year
fields.description: Year AD (astronomers' numbering is the same for AD years).

fields.name: calendar
fields.description: Calendar of the civil dates in this row: Julian to 1582, Gregorian from 1583 (the Gregorian calendar began on 15 October 1582).

fields.name: real_equinox
fields.description: The real spring (March) equinox, Jerusalem local time. Civil date written YYYY-MM-DD, in the calendar named in `calendar`.

fields.name: real_equinox_jdn
fields.description: Julian Day Number of `real_equinox` (the day that begins at noon UT on that date): one count of days with no calendar to doubt.

fields.name: real_full_moon
fields.description: The first real full moon on or after that equinox, Jerusalem local time. Civil date written YYYY-MM-DD, in the calendar named in `calendar`.

fields.name: real_full_moon_jdn
fields.description: Julian Day Number of `real_full_moon` (the day that begins at noon UT on that date): one count of days with no calendar to doubt.

fields.name: real_full_moon_time_jerusalem
fields.description: Time of that full moon, Jerusalem local mean time, HH:MM.

fields.name: aleppo_easter
fields.description: Easter by the 1997 Aleppo proposal: the Sunday after the real full moon, reckoned at Jerusalem's meridian. Civil date written YYYY-MM-DD, in the calendar named in `calendar`.

fields.name: aleppo_easter_jdn
fields.description: Julian Day Number of `aleppo_easter` (the day that begins at noon UT on that date): one count of days with no calendar to doubt.

fields.name: julian_tables_full_moon
fields.description: The Easter full moon of the Julian (Alexandrian) tables, which the Orthodox churches still use. Civil date written YYYY-MM-DD, in the calendar named in `calendar`.

fields.name: julian_tables_full_moon_jdn
fields.description: Julian Day Number of `julian_tables_full_moon` (the day that begins at noon UT on that date): one count of days with no calendar to doubt.

fields.name: julian_tables_full_moon_julian_calendar
fields.description: The same full moon in the Julian calendar, the calendar the tables run in.

fields.name: julian_tables_days_from_real
fields.description: Days from the real full moon to the Julian tables' full moon (positive: the tables run late).

fields.name: orthodox_easter
fields.description: Easter by the Julian tables: Orthodox Easter (and every church's Easter before 1583). Civil date written YYYY-MM-DD, in the calendar named in `calendar`.

fields.name: orthodox_easter_jdn
fields.description: Julian Day Number of `orthodox_easter` (the day that begins at noon UT on that date): one count of days with no calendar to doubt.

fields.name: orthodox_easter_julian_calendar
fields.description: The same Easter in the Julian calendar.

fields.name: gregorian_tables_full_moon
fields.description: From 1583: the Easter full moon of the Gregorian tables. Empty before 1583. Civil date written YYYY-MM-DD, in the calendar named in `calendar`.

fields.name: gregorian_tables_full_moon_jdn
fields.description: Julian Day Number of `gregorian_tables_full_moon` (the day that begins at noon UT on that date): one count of days with no calendar to doubt.

fields.name: gregorian_tables_days_from_real
fields.description: From 1583: days from the real full moon to the Gregorian tables' full moon.

fields.name: western_easter
fields.description: Western Easter: by the Gregorian tables from 1583, by the Julian tables before. Civil date written YYYY-MM-DD, in the calendar named in `calendar`.

fields.name: western_easter_jdn
fields.description: Julian Day Number of `western_easter` (the day that begins at noon UT on that date): one count of days with no calendar to doubt.

fields.name: western_matches_aleppo
fields.description: yes when Western Easter falls on the Aleppo (astronomical) date.

fields.name: orthodox_matches_aleppo
fields.description: yes when Orthodox Easter falls on the Aleppo date.

fields.name: western_orthodox_weeks_apart
fields.description: Weeks from Western to Orthodox Easter: 0, 1, 4 or 5.
